newsitem.title: USA: Chevron extends healthcare benefits to gay partners.
newsitem.headline: Chevron extends healthcare benefits to gay partners.

text.p: Chevron Corp. will become the first major U.S. oil company to extend domestic partner benefits to most of its American employees, regardless of sexual orientation, a spokesman said on Thursday.

The 117-year-old company follows in the footsteps of Bank of America and other San Francisco-area firms that have offered similar programmes since the city passed an ordinance in 1996 requiring companies doing business with the city to offer equal benefits to employees' partners, whether "straight" or same-sex.

"This helps us attract and retain the best people to better serve our diverse customer base, which is essential for our continued business success," Ron Kiskis, vice president of human resources said.
Under Chevron's plan, which takes effect in January 1998, employees will be able to enroll partners of the same or opposite sex, as well as the partner's eligible children, the company said.
Benefits offered will include medical, dental, dependent life insurance, relocation and leave-time for bereavement or care of sick partners, it said.
San Francisco-based Chevron Corp. has about 26,250 employees in the United States and 35,310 worldwide.

The benefits will apply to all of Chevron's U.S. employees except for about 5,000 who work for subsidiaries. Managers of the subsidiaries will decide what benefits will be offered to those employees, Chevron said.

About 8,000 to 10,000 private-sector businesses have contracts and do work for San Francisco, according to Jeff Sheehy, who helped write the ordinance and serves as president of the Harvey Milk Lesbian/Gay/Bisexual Democratic Club.
"It's fantastic," Sheehy said when told of Chevron's announcement. "Chevron is leading the way in what is traditionally a conservative industry."
Should companies fail to offer or promise equal health benefits to same-sex partners by June 1997, they would be barred from bidding for city contracts.
